title: END-TO-END DEMONSTRATOR RADAR FOR SPACE OBJECT DETECTION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop and validate an end-to-end demonstrator of a multistatic radar system for space object detection and tracking using cooperative and non-cooperative signals from diverse satellites. The activity evaluates the integration within NewSpace LEO constellations to support advanced surveillance, monitoring, and situational awareness services.Description:  The activity focuses on the development and validation of a complete end-to-end testbed demonstrator for multistatic radar object detection. The system shall operate by receiving and processing reflected signals from multiple satellites, regardless of whether they are designed forcooperative use (e.g. hosted beacons or known signal providers) or non cooperative (e.g. opportunistic use of signals transmitted for other purposes). The aim is to build a prototype capable of operating in representative environments, addressing the practical implementation of hardware and software elements, as well as system integration within NewSpace LEO constellations.  The system designed in this activity focuses on detecting, localizing, and tracking space objects through the reception and processing of reflected signals. Theactivity targets to validate detection performance in controlled settings, assess spatial coverage and scalability, and propose strategies for real-world deployment. A key objective is to enable seamless integration into existing or planned LEO constellations viaflexible architectures, such as hosted payloads or onboard processing modules. The use of a multilayer sensing approach will also be evaluated. The results of this activity aims to contribute to space capabilities in Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and Space Traffic Management (STM), Resilience and Security of Space Assets. The system developed in this activity shall be designed to detectand correlate both direct and reflected signals, supported by the development of advanced algorithms for object detection, tracking,and clutter suppression. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Provide a comprehensive state-of-the-artand feasibility baseline to drive the design of the radar demonstrator architecture. - - - - Provide a complete end-to-end systemarchitecture specification and a technical reference model for demonstrator implementation. Develop a modular, end-to-end software simulator thatmodels the transmission processing chain, signal-object interaction, and receiver-side processing. Develop the functional breadboardimplementations of both the transmitter and receiver chains. Execute a controlled environment validation of thebreadboards and provide experimental validation results. Deliverables: Breadboard, Prototype, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTPWork Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating stateswill be known at tender issue.

title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: GT1D-613SY - METHODOLOGY TO UPDATE OPERATIONAL MODELS OF A SPACECRAFT SYSTEM (EXPRO+)
description: Simulation models developed at design, AIT and operations phases shall be recalibrated based on the flight experience. Currently, during operation, the predictive simulations performed by design, AIT and operations teams with simulators are not fully connected toflight telemetry. Therefore, the simulators do not reflect the real state of the spacecraft and the lessons learned are not transferred to the models for the next spacecraft. The activity aims at streamlining the process, enhancing the fidelity and representativeness of the simulation models and reducing the effort for models update and reusability. In this activity, to implement the correction of the model, an assessment to define the origin of the deviation shall be made considering the latest advancement in digitalization, model calibration and synchronization, leveraging the concepts of digital twins' spacecraft. Furthermore, state of the art approaches of surrogate modelling, AI and Machine Learning shall be considered to enhance representativeness and fidelity. The experimentation plan shall be extended in a multidisciplinary way, to improve the method, including in-flight data, and to prepare multidisciplinary optimization to improve operations, future design and reduce the margins.

title: LOW COST AND HIGH EFFICIENCY DEPLOYABLE RADIATOR FLAP FOR TELECOM CONSTELLATION SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low cost and high efficiency deployable radiator flap based on 2-phase technology (based on evaporation-condensation of a fluid to transport heat) for satellites constellations.Description: A small telecom platform operating in LEO (Low Earth Orbit) will require additional surface area to radiate heat, hence necessitating the deployment of radiator flap(s). These radiator flaps will need to be low cost and will utilize two-phase equipment to efficiently transport heat from the main radiator to theflaps. This activity will assess the use of flexible heat pipes or low-cost loop heat pipes. Several technologies will be evaluatedand the one that offers the best flexibility and scalability for high aspect ratio satellites will be selected. The assembly of the2-phase equipment with the flap will also have to be studied, as well as the flap technology itself (material, coating) to meet mass, performance and integration requirements (stowed and deployed configuration). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation. - Technologies trade off review and baseline selection. - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator. - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
